title: HR Hiring Flow Automation with Claude
tagline: From portal filter to approved pitch, with a recruiter in control of every decision
audience: HR operations and talent acquisition teams, HR technology and enterprise IT automation engineers, and the network and platform teams that build and host these workflows in India and worldwide
prerequisites: Basic Python and the command line
Working knowledge of your organisation's hiring process and job portal exports
Familiarity with JSON and REST APIs
Familiarity with an AI coding assistant is helpful, not required
outcomes: Map a real hiring flow from portal filtering to pitch and decide which steps a model may propose and which only a person may approve
Set up Claude Code, the Claude Agent SDK and an MCP server that exposes portal exports and a candidate store as tools with strict JSON outputs
Build a validated candidate profile pipeline that captures experience, location, salary ask and preferred working hours with unknowns marked, never guessed
Automate call preparation, scheduling and consented recording through Twilio Programmable Voice, and score English proficiency and fit from transcripts with cited evidence

Ship an approval-gated pitch generator delivered by email with PII minimisation, consent tracking, prompt injection defences, fairness checks, an append-only audit log and a ServiceNow onboarding handoff

modules.title: The hiring flow and the automation baseline
topics: Mapping the client flow end to end: portal filter, download, screening call, assessment, pitch, offer and onboarding handoff
Which steps Claude may propose and which a recruiter must approve: shortlist, outreach, pitch, salary discussion
Candidate data obligations: consent, purpose limitation and retention under India's DPDP Act and GDPR
The teaching pattern: Claude plans and drafts, deterministic code executes, a human approves, everything is logged
modules.lab: Stand up the lab with Docker Compose, load a synthetic portal export and draw the current versus target hiring flow with a Mermaid diagram.
modules.deliverable: Hiring flow map with approval points marked.

modules.title: Setting up Claude Code, the Agent SDK and MCP for hiring
topics: A Claude Code project with a CLAUDE.md that encodes hiring policy, forbidden actions and output schemas
The Claude Agent SDK in Python: sessions, tool use, structured JSON outputs validated by Pydantic
An MCP server exposing read-only portal export tools and a write-gated candidate store on PostgreSQL
Secrets handling for portal, telephony and ServiceNow credentials outside prompts and repositories
modules.lab: Build the hiring MCP server, connect it to Claude Code and have the agent list candidates through a tool call that returns validated JSON.
modules.deliverable: Working Claude Code, Agent SDK and MCP workspace.

modules.title: Sourcing: filtering and downloading from the portal of choice
topics: Portal exports as the source of truth: CSV and XLSX downloads and sanctioned APIs, respecting each portal's terms of service
Claude translates a job requisition into deterministic filter rules; Python applies them and reports what was excluded and why
Deduplication across portals by email and phone with normalisation, and rejected-row reporting
Provenance on every record: portal, export file, row number and timestamp
modules.lab: Implement the export importer and filter engine with pytest coverage, then compare the agent's proposed filters against the recruiter's own shortlist.
modules.deliverable: Portal import and filter pipeline with provenance.

modules.title: Candidate profile schema and resume extraction
topics: A typed CandidateProfile: experience, skills, current and preferred location, salary ask, notice period, preferred working hours
Claude extracts fields from resume text into the schema with a confidence per field; unknowns are marked, never guessed
Treating resume text as untrusted input: tool-free extraction, schema validation and rejection of out-of-schema content
Human review queue for low-confidence fields
modules.lab: Run extraction over fifty synthetic resumes, measure field accuracy against ground truth and route the low-confidence fields to review.

modules.title: Calling candidates: scripts, scheduling and consented recording
topics: Claude drafts a per-candidate call script from the requisition and the profile; the recruiter runs the call
Deterministic scheduling of call slots by candidate time zone and preferred working hours, with reminders by email
Twilio Programmable Voice for outbound calls, recorded consent announcements and recording retrieval
Transcription stored against the candidate record with timestamps and the recruiter's own notes
modules.lab: Place a call to the sandbox number, capture consent and a transcript, and attach both to the candidate record through the MCP write tool.

modules.title: Assessing English proficiency, experience, location, salary ask and hours
topics: A rubric-driven scoring agent: English proficiency on CEFR-aligned bands with quoted transcript evidence for each score
Deterministic checks for experience years, location, preferred working hours against the shift, and salary ask against the approved band
Structured JSON score cards with confidence; low confidence and disagreement with the recruiter routed to a human
Fairness checks: scoring only on job-relevant criteria, with protected attributes excluded from the prompt
modules.lab: Score twenty synthetic transcripts, compare against two human raters and tune the rubric until agreement is acceptable.

modules.title: Pitching the role: drafts within approved talking points
topics: Claude drafts a personalised pitch from the score card, the role and a versioned library of approved talking points
Hard constraints enforced in code: salary band, location, working hours and benefits the company has actually approved
Delivery by email templates only after recruiter approval; tracking replies against the candidate record
Objection handling notes for the recruiter, never automated negotiation
modules.lab: Generate pitches for the top ten candidates, prove the generator refuses an out-of-band salary, and route each draft through approval.

modules.title: Guardrails, approvals and audit for hiring automation
topics: PII minimisation with consent and retention tracking: what the model sees, what the database stores, deletion on request
Prompt injection defences for resumes and transcripts, with tests that inject instructions and confirm they are ignored
Approval gates with named approvers for shortlist, outreach and pitch; append-only audit log in PostgreSQL
Bias monitoring on score distributions and a recruiter override path that is always logged
modules.lab: Attack the pipeline with an injected resume and an unapproved pitch, watch both fail closed, and reconstruct one candidate's journey from the audit log.

modules.title: Orchestration, ServiceNow handoff and CI
topics: The pipeline as a FastAPI service with explicit state per candidate and idempotent reruns
ServiceNow Table API records for onboarding and access requests opened on acceptance, with Flow Designer notifications
GitHub pull requests for every prompt, rubric and schema change; GitHub Actions running pytest and evaluation sets
Operational dashboard: time to shortlist, call completion, approval turnaround and override rate
modules.lab: Open a pull request that changes the scoring rubric, let GitHub Actions run the evaluation set, and trigger the ServiceNow onboarding record for an accepted candidate.
modules.deliverable: Orchestrated pipeline with CI and ServiceNow handoff.

modules.title: Capstone: requisition to approved shortlist
topics: One job requisition in, one approved and documented shortlist out, with no candidate contacted without approval
Acceptance review: accuracy, fairness evidence, audit completeness and a limitations statement
Team demo and handover runbook for recruiters and IT

capstone: A repeatable hiring pipeline that filters and downloads candidates from the portal of choice, prepares and records consented screening calls, scores English proficiency, experience, location, salary ask and preferred working hours with cited evidence, and drafts a pitch that reaches a candidate only after a recruiter approves it, with every step in an audit log.

narration: hook

Three hundred applications land in the job portal overnight. Your recruiters have two days, one phone each, and a hiring manager who wants a shortlist by Friday. Every profile has to be filtered, downloaded, called, judged and pitched, and every one of those steps is done by hand.
hook

What if an agent filtered the portal, downloaded the profiles, prepared every screening call, scored English proficiency, experience, location, salary ask and working hours against the role, and drafted the pitch, while a person made every decision that matters? That is hiring flow automation, done with Claude, done safely.
intro
Gennoor Tech presents HR Hiring Flow Automation with Claude.
story

One job requisition in. One approved, documented shortlist out. You build the hiring pipeline in ten modules across three days, and every module is something you can test, review and demonstrate. Claude plans, drafts and explains. Deterministic Python code executes. A recruiter approves every outreach and every pitch. And everything is logged.
path0

You begin by mapping the real hiring flow, from the job portal of your choice to the onboarding ticket, and by deciding which steps a model may propose and which only a person may approve. Then you set up Claude Code with a project file that encodes hiring policy, the Claude Agent S D K in Python, and a Model Context Protocol server that exposes your portal exports and candidate store as tools with strict J S O N outputs.
path0

Next comes sourcing. You filter and download candidate data from portal exports and sanctioned portal A P I endpoints, validate every row with Pydantic, deduplicate across portals, and record where every record came from. A typed candidate profile captures experience, location, salary ask and preferred working hours, extracted from resumes with a confidence per field. Unknowns are marked, never guessed.
path1

On day two you reach the candidate. Claude drafts a call script from the role and the profile, and a deterministic scheduler books a slot in the candidate's preferred hours and places the call through Twilio Programmable Voice, with recorded consent and a transcript stored against the record. The script is a proposal. The recruiter runs the call, and nothing dials until they say yes.
path2

Then assessment. A rubric-driven agent scores English proficiency from the transcript on C E F R aligned bands, checks experience, location, working hours and salary ask against the requisition, and cites the exact lines that justify each score. Low confidence routes to a human. A pitch generator then drafts a personalised pitch within approved talking points and the approved salary band. Ask it to promise a number outside the band and it refuses. And nothing is sent until the recruiter approves it.
path3

Day three is control. You build the guardrails specific to hiring: P I I minimisation, consent and retention tracking, prompt injection defences for untrusted resume and transcript text, fairness checks on score distributions, and an append-only audit log in PostgreSQL. Every shortlist, every outreach and every pitch passes through an approval gate with a named approver, and every override is recorded.
path3

Finally orchestration. The pipeline runs as a FastAPI service with pytest coverage. Every prompt, rubric and schema change goes through a GitHub pull request, and GitHub Actions runs the evaluation set before it merges. When a candidate accepts, a ServiceNow record is opened through the Table A P I so onboarding and access requests start the same day.
labs

Every lab uses synthetic candidates, synthetic portal exports and a sandbox telephony number. You will watch a resume try to inject instructions into the scorer and fail. You will see the gate block a pitch that quotes the wrong salary. And you will trace one candidate from portal row to onboarding ticket, event by event, in the audit log.
stats
Ten course modules. Three days, hands-on. Five fit criteria scored with cited evidence. And zero candidates contacted without a recruiter's approval.
who

This course is for H R operations and talent acquisition teams, H R technology and enterprise I T automation engineers, and the network and platform teams asked to build and host these workflows, in India and worldwide. You need basic Python, a working knowledge of your hiring process, and nothing more. No prior agent experience is required.
